title: Connector fallback cases and customer threads — Jun 18 2026
content:
Meeting: Connector fallback cases sync
Date: 2026-06-18
Attendees: Priya Nair (owner), Ethan Park, Maya Chen, Omar Haddad, Jake (support), Aria (solutions eng)
Context / why this doc: we keep seeing intermittent customer reports where the local connector falls back to the slower /cpu-compatible runtime (or the remote fallback route) unexpectedly during spikes. This doc collects observed cases, quick repros, what we tried, and next actions for the week.

Top-level summary:
- Two production customers (Acadia Bio, Meridian Forms) reported repeat fallbacks between 06/10–06/17. Impact: increased latency from ~60ms/token to 300–900ms/token and token cost >2x for affected routes.
- Common signal: "fallback" flagged in runtime trace, concurrent connection count spikes, transient EBS latency (customer VPC) or node memory pressure on the on-prem appliance.
- Immediate mitigations applied: temporary route pinning to smaller-quant model, raising connector threads to 12 for Meridian, and enabling aggressive KV-cache warmup for Acadia.

Detailed case notes
1) Acadia Bio — 2026-06-12 incident (primary)
- Symptoms: sustained fallback for ~18 minutes; customer saw timeouts in app.
- Observed logs: connector reported "fallback: kernel-compat" at 12:13:04Z. Host dmesg shows intermittent soft errors from the NVMe array (latency spikes).
- What we tried: re-provisioned connector instance, temporarily routed traffic to dedicated pool in us-west-2, set mem_limit +20% on connector container.
- Root-cause hypothesis: noisy neighbour on the customer's NVMe causing slow disk reads for checkpoint restoration during an autoscale event.
- Follow-ups: Solutions to capture on-host iostat/blkparse sampling (action: Ethan). Ask customer for scheduled maintenance windows and disk SMART logs (action: Aria).

2) Meridian Forms — 2026-06-15 recurring fallbacks
- Symptoms: fallback occurs after ~500 concurrent chat sessions begin, frequency scales with concurrent LRU eviction pressure.
- Observed logs: connector logs show KV-cache misses spike and then fallback when cache warmup exceeds per-req latency budget.
- What we tried: increased connector threadpool and raised batch_window to 15ms for a subset of routes — helped reduce fallback frequency but increased per-request p95 in some short-lived flows.
- Root-cause hypothesis: cache priming not aggressive enough on rapid burst workloads; configuration defaults are tuned for stable long-running streams not massive short bursts.
- Follow-ups: iterate on warmup heuristics in the connector (PR 198 references experiment), add a fast-path to pin first-n requests to a warm pool (action: Priya + Omar).

Other customer threads (summary)
- Epsilon Logistics: fallback after a user-triggered model swap; noticed a race where old KV cache eviction finished after new model boot, leading to inconsistent compatibility check.
- Atlas Retail: network MTU mismatch in onprem appliance resulted in occasional TLS re-handshakes and connector keepalive resets — fallbacks aligned with resets.

What we tried across incidents (short bits)
- Increased connector memory headroom (mem_limit +10–30%).
- Temporary route pinning to smaller/quantized variants to keep tail latency bounded.
- Manual cache pre-warm scripts run prior to expected spikes for two customers.
- Quick telemetry patch to log "fallback_reason" and last-5 cache keys for correlation (deployed 2026-06-16).

Open technical hypotheses (ranked)
1) Disk/IO stalls on customer onprem (high confidence for Acadia). Action: add iostat sampling + automated upload. Owner: Ethan. ETA: 2026-06-22.
2) KV-cache warmup heuristic fails under high-burst concurrency; conservative defaults are too slow. Action: experiment on warmup aggressiveness + short-circuit first-n. Owner: Priya/Omar. ETA: prototype 2026-06-24.
3) Connector thread starvation during GC pauses in Java-based sidecars (lower confidence). Action: gather GC logs from affected customers. Owner: Maya. ETA: 2026-06-23.
4) Network MTU / TLS rehandshake causing transient disconnects leading to fallback. Action: publish troubleshooting checklist for customers and run MTU checks during onboarding. Owner: Aria. ETA: 2026-06-25.

Action items (concrete)
- Ethan: add iostat/blkparse sampler to acme-agent and wire an S3 upload; add alert rule for NVMe latency > 50ms sustained (ETA 06/22).
- Priya + Omar: branch warming experiment (fast-path 'first-5' request pinning + aggressive KV prefetch), run load test against Meridian synthetic; share results on 06/24.
- Maya: collect GC logs from customers where sidecar is Java; provide parsing template for SRE support (ETA 06/23).
- Aria: coordinate with Acadia to get SMART logs and maintenance schedule; run MTU check with Atlas (ETA 06/21).
- Jake (support): escalate DEPLOY-3421 to SEs for immediate customer comms and post-mortem scheduling.

Short checklist for standby responders
- If fallback observed: (1) check connector fallback_reason in runtime trace (2) check KV-cache hit rate over last 60s (3) check node memory pressure and iostat (4) if disk latency > 20ms, advise route pin to quantized model.

Telemetry / logging improvements (near-term)
- Log the connector "fallback_reason" with upstream latency bucket and last-5 keys. Done (small patch deployed 06/16).
- Add a synthetic canary that simulates 600 parallel short chat sessions to detect warmup weaknesses. Owner: Omar. ETA 06/26.

Customer comms notes (for CS/solutions)
- Draft note to Acadia: explain noisy NVMe hypothesis, share temporary mitigation (route pin + mem headroom), request SMART logs and proposed maintenance window. (Aria to send by 06/19).
- Draft note to Meridian: outline warmup improvement plan and timeline; offer to run load-days to validate config. (Priya to coordinate).

Risk table (quick)
- Risk: temporary route pin increases token cost. Mitigation: estimate cost delta and put Finance on alert for large spikes.
- Risk: aggressive warmup increases average p95 for long-running streams. Mitigation: A/B on low-traffic routes first.

Unresolved questions
- Can we instrument disk latency at 1s granularity without causing extra IO on constrained customers? (Ethan to prototype.)
- Is there a universal heuristic for 'first-n warm pin' that works across model sizes and hardware? (Priya/Omar experiment needed.)

References and quick links
- Jira: DEPLOY-3421 (customer fallbacks)
- PR: private-deploy/pull/198 (warmup experiments)
- Confluence: Node Tiling Notes (background on LRU eviction patterns)

Next sync: weekly install triage, Thu 2026-06-24 09:30 PT. Will review experiment results and customer SMART logs.

Notes to self:
- When writing runbook entry, include explicit command snippets to capture iostat and nvme-cli output and a one-liner to tail fallback_reason logs. Keep the runbook < 1 page, run-test scripts in repo.
- Keep a short FAQ for CS around "why did my model fallback" with three common causes and exact commands to run.

--- end doc
